# Lab 5.2: JavaScript UDFs

## What We Are Going to Do
Write a JavaScript UDF, then load an external JavaScript library from Cloud Storage and use it inside the function.

## Steps

1. **[SQL] A simple JavaScript UDF.**


<div style="margin:18px 0;border:1px solid #334155;border-radius:8px;overflow:hidden;">
<div style="background:#243244;color:#DBEAFE;padding:7px 12px;font-family:Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif;font-size:12px;font-weight:700;">
CODE • SQL
</div>
<pre style="margin:0;background:#111827;color:#F3F4F6;padding:16px;overflow-x:auto;white-space:pre;font-family:Consolas,'Cascadia Code',monospace;font-size:14px;line-height:1.55;"><code><span style="color:#F3F4F6;">CREATE TEMP FUNCTION title_case(s STRING)
RETURNS STRING
LANGUAGE js AS r"""
  if (s === null) return null;
  return s.toLowerCase().split(' ').map(w =&gt; w.charAt(0).toUpperCase() + w.slice(1)).join(' ');
""";

SELECT title_case('hello BIGQUERY world') AS fixed;</span>
</code></pre>
</div>


2. **[CLI] Upload a small library to Cloud Storage.**


<div style="margin:18px 0;border:1px solid #334155;border-radius:8px;overflow:hidden;">
<div style="background:#243244;color:#DBEAFE;padding:7px 12px;font-family:Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif;font-size:12px;font-weight:700;">
CODE • BASH
</div>
<pre style="margin:0;background:#111827;color:#F3F4F6;padding:16px;overflow-x:auto;white-space:pre;font-family:Consolas,'Cascadia Code',monospace;font-size:14px;line-height:1.55;"><code><span style="color:#F3F4F6;">export BUCKET=$PROJECT_ID-bq-labs
cat &gt; slug.js &lt;&lt;'EOF'
function slugify(text) {
  return text.toString().toLowerCase().trim()
    .replace(/[^a-z0-9]+/g, '-').replace(/^-+|-+$/g, '');
}
EOF
gcloud storage cp slug.js gs://$BUCKET/js/slug.js</span>
</code></pre>
</div>


3. **[SQL] Use the library in a persistent UDF.** Replace `YOUR_BUCKET`.


<div style="margin:18px 0;border:1px solid #334155;border-radius:8px;overflow:hidden;">
<div style="background:#243244;color:#DBEAFE;padding:7px 12px;font-family:Segoe UI,Arial,sans-serif;font-size:12px;font-weight:700;">
CODE • SQL
</div>
<pre style="margin:0;background:#111827;color:#F3F4F6;padding:16px;overflow-x:auto;white-space:pre;font-family:Consolas,'Cascadia Code',monospace;font-size:14px;line-height:1.55;"><code><span style="color:#F3F4F6;">CREATE OR REPLACE FUNCTION lab05.slug(s STRING)
RETURNS STRING
LANGUAGE js
OPTIONS (library = ['gs://YOUR_BUCKET/js/slug.js'])
AS r"""
  return s === null ? null : slugify(s);
""";

SELECT name, lab05.slug(name) AS url_slug
FROM `bigquery-public-data.thelook_ecommerce.products` LIMIT 10;</span>
</code></pre>
</div>


4. **[Console] Compare speed.** Open **Execution details** for step 3. JavaScript UDFs run slower than SQL. Use them only when SQL cannot do the job.

## Expected Result

| Thing | Reality |
|---|---|
| Inline JS | Works with `LANGUAGE js` |
| External library | Loaded from `gs://` with `library` |
| Output | `url_slug` such as `classic-cotton-tee` |
| Rule | Prefer SQL UDFs for speed |
